title: Rasch Analysis of AI Safety Benchmark Items: Diagnosing Misfit, Unidimensionality, and Item Quality

original_idea.body:
# Rasch Analysis of AI Safety Benchmark Items: Diagnosing Misfit, Unidimensionality, and Item Quality in Existing Safety Evaluation Sets

**Problem:** Existing AI safety benchmarks are assembled without formal item analysis. It is unknown whether their items form a coherent unidimensional scale, which items are misfitting, and whether benchmark scores reflect a single underlying 'safety' construct or a patchwork of unrelated behaviors.

**Direction:** Apply the Rasch measurement model (using the R package eRm or TAM) to response data from a publicly available AI safety benchmark with binary pass/fail items. Estimate item difficulty parameters and person (model) ability parameters. Compute infit and outfit MNSQ statistics to flag misfitting items. Run a Principal Component Analysis of Rasch residuals to assess unidimensionality. Produce a Wright map showing item difficulty distribution relative to model 'ability.' Interpret what misfitting items have in common (e.g., topic, format) and what this implies about the construct being measured.

**Why it matters:** Rasch analysis has been standard practice in educational and clinical measurement for decades for exactly these quality-control purposes. If AI safety benchmarks contain misfitting items or measure multiple unrelated constructs, their scores conflate unrelated behaviors and mislead decision-makers. This analysis requires only R and a matrix of model-by-item pass/fail responses, which are publicly available for several benchmarks.

**Relevant context:** IRT/Rasch has already been applied to AI benchmark evaluation (arxiv 2306.10512, which proposes adaptive testing for AI). The 'From Static Benchmarks to Adaptive Testing' paper explicitly calls for item-level psychometric analysis. Rasch fit statistics use MNSQ thresholds of 0.7-1.3 for acceptable fit. The eRm and TAM packages in R implement full Rasch analyses. Unidimensionality is a prerequisite for score interpretability; violation means the single summary score is meaningless.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: misfitting items and multidimensionality undermine benchmark score interpretability, which in turn undermines safety decisions. The risk mechanism is named but the chain has a gap: diagnosing the problem does not fix it without benchmark revision.

low_compute.reasoning: Rasch analysis in R on an existing response matrix. Minimal compute, CPU-only.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Rasch analysis in R with eRm is well-documented with tutorials. Understanding infit/outfit and PCA of residuals requires some psychometric background but is guided by clear thresholds (0.7-1.3 MNSQ).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: apply Rasch to one benchmark, produce Wright map, flag misfitting items. A single well-defined analysis with concrete visual outputs.

quick_reasoning: Directly addresses safety benchmark item quality with comprehensive Rasch analysis; safety relevance is immediate for construct validity of safety measurement.
